recipe.description: Header/beam inventory and continuum peak search in all 2D images (>5 sigma local maxima, MAD noise)
Extract spectra at the N/S positions from every cube (peak pixel; 1" mean for Xb4b); cubes read via memmap

Blind line search: boxcar matched filter (150 km/s), robust MAD noise, 4 sigma at nuclei; later 5 sigma, widths 100/200/300 km/s in all region spectra, excluding 30 MHz at spw edges; candidate assignment from Splatalogue within +-120 km/s of 2780 km/s
Systemic velocity: moment-1 of HCO+/HCN spectra at N and S peak pixels, radio convention
Moment-0 maps (vsys+-350 km/s; +-450..150 wing windows) for HCO+/HCN in every OUS; peaks per tracer (S/N>8, within primary beam FWHM); objective region list from Xb4d

Standard line table: for each target line, region, cube: peak-pixel and 1.5" aperture spectra (pbcor), local polynomial baseline from line-free channels (order 1; 2 for H13CN), integrated intensity over fixed window, peak, rms per channel, W50, single Gaussian fit, empirical null noise from emission-free pixels (300 per cube); status detected (>=5 sigma and peak>=3 sigma), marginal (3-5), limit (3 sigma); edge-flagged within 100 MHz of spw edges

The response to injected differences is monotonic (HCN 2-1: f=1.25,1.5,2,3 -> recovered/recovered(f=1) = 1.23, 1.46, 1.89, 2.70), so factor-1.25 changes are visible in the same line, but a species ratio (e.g. HCN/HCO+ 2-1) can be biased by a factor 0.45 (2-1) or 0.93 (4-3). Minimum detectable N-S difference in a ladder ratio: ~30-40% (cross-band 14% x sqrt2 and ensemble spread), a 2-1 N-S HCN/HCO+ contrast is not measurable (N and S amplitudes correlated, corr ~0.8)

results.quantity: Q1b: Disk 3-2 deficit: resolved-out flux vs low excitation (parametric uv-hole model, Band 5 2-1 vs Band 6 Xb4f 3-2)
results.value: Disk-mask 3-2/2-1 (Tb) relative to the compact (N, S, deblended and 10" matched) value: HCO+ 0.59 (no zero-level correction) / 0.64 (ring correction) [0.265 vs 0.451]; HCN 0.10 / 0.43 [0.034 vs 0.358]. A Gaussian disk of FWHM th loses a fraction of its brightness exp[-(pi th B_min/lambda)^2/(4 ln2)] with B_min = 8.7 m (7-m array shadowing; both maps have B_max ~ lambda/theta_maj ~ 40 m, i.e. compact-array-like beams): deficit 0.76/0.67/0.58/0.49/0.33/0.18 for th = 10/12/14/16/20/25" (B_min 15 m: 0.44/0.31/0.20/0.12/0.04/0.006); the HCO+ deficit is reproduced by th = 13-14" (B_min 8.7 m) or 7-8" (15 m) -- a natural scale for the structure in the mask -- so the HCO+ disk deficit is fully consistent with the same excitation as the nuclei plus missing short spacings in Xb4f (MRS ~26" at 1.1 mm vs ~40" at 1.7 mm for B_min 8.7 m). Not consistent with the model alone: HCN (deficit 0.10 without correction, th=17-29" needed) and the double ratio (HCN/HCO+ 3-2)/(HCN/HCO+ 2-1) = 0.13 (none) / 0.54 (ring) in the disk vs 0.77 (N) and 0.76 (S) at 10": if HCN and HCO+ share distribution and recovery this double ratio is recovery-independent, so the disk HCN 3-2 is weak relative to HCO+ 3-2 (or HCN is more compact) -- but its value depends entirely on the ring zero level (0.13 vs 0.54). The robust disk number is HCN/HCO+ 2-1 = 0.47-0.50 (+-0.01 stat, +-0.03 zero level) vs 0.62 (N), 0.56 (S) at the same 10" beam, i.e. 15-25% lower; the disk 3-2 ratio is reported only as a lower limit in recovery (HCO+ 3-2/2-1 >= 0.265-0.287 true ratio)

results.quantity: Q3b: HCN blue-side excess at Soutflow over k*HCO+ and its independence from blends
results.value: HCN = k*HCO+ fitted on 2575-2875 km/s gives k=0.574+-0.019 (Michiyama South-OF-Blue position: 0.634+-0.021). The residual in HCN-frame 2375-2575 km/s is 0.164+-0.016 Jy/beam km/s = 57% of the HCN flux there (0.288); it is one broad bump (Gaussian centre 2497+-11, FWHM 211 km/s) of ~1 mJy/beam, 5-6 sigma per 50 km/s bin. Same excess in independent products: Xb4d tapered cube 0.238+-0.013 (73% of HCN), Xb4b smoothed to 1.05" 0.087+-0.026 (42%), significant (3 sigma per bin) only in 2500-2575. Blend test independent of the HCN wing: LTE forward models (Tex 15-120 K, line weights nu^3*S*mu2*exp(-Eu/T), HCO+-shaped or box velocity profile) of every in-band line of CH3NH2 (158 lines), CH3OH (59), CH2NH (54), CH3CHO (161), CH3SH (104) fitted to all other Band-6 channels at the same position (HCN/HCO+/SO channels and HOC+ masked) give no detection (A/sigma -1.3..+1.9) and 2-sigma upper bounds on the blend in HCN-frame 2375-2475 / 2475-2575 / 2575-2675 km/s of <=18% / <=10% / <=11% of the HCN flux (sum over species of the maximum over T and profile; Michiyama position <=37% / 13% / 11%); in the 2275-2375 bin (HCN weak, 0.6 mJy/beam) the bound is only <=42%. The CH3OH line at 263.728 GHz sky (rest 266.196 GHz, 3(2,1)-3(0,3)E) has log A=-8.5, ~1e-4 of the in-band CH3OH lines, so thermal CH3OH cannot contribute. HDO 2(2,0)-3(1,3) (266.161 GHz, Eu 157 K) has no other in-band line and is untestable (implausible but not excluded). Blend-corrected wing ratio therefore = R_obs*(1-f) with f<=0.1-0.2: e.g. blue half 1.24 -> 1.0-1.24. The earlier "10-15%" number is now derived (upper limit), not assumed. [Scope correction, team-a Q4c: SO ratios are central 9.4x6.3" beam averages, not nuclear; Trot < 12-25 K holds only if SO is as extended in its 24 K and 51 K lines; compact warm SO (Trot >= 30-80 K) is not excluded, so 'no shock signature at the nuclei' is withdrawn for SO.]
results.uncertainty: k +-0.02; blend fraction <=0.10-0.18 (2 sigma upper bound)

Significance (ln-ratio z, 10% systematic floor per aperture): blue half Soutflow(centroid) vs S z=+6 (Xb4d)/+9 (Xb4b): HIGHER than S, robust; vs N +0.5 (Xb4d)/-1.0 (Xb4b) and vs Bridge -0.4: NOT significantly different (the M18 aperture gives +1.5 vs N). (1) The "sharp red edge" is NOT diagnostic: the 25%-of-peak red edge is 2867-2872 km/s at Soutflow, 2867-2889 at S and 2832-2889 along the N-S cut at x=-0.2": the lobe has no gas redder than the S disk red edge, i.e. it is one-sided (blue only), not specifically cut at Vsys+100. (2) E-W rotation gradient at the S declination 35 km/s/arcsec (v0=2795): expected line sigma for disk gas on the minor axis from beam smearing ~62 km/s, observed 130-150 (HCN) / 112-135 (HCO+) at Soutflow vs 24 at the W control (-4.4,-4.5) and 49-104 at the mirror N of S: the broadening is not rotation smearing. (3) HCO+/HCN peak velocity at Soutflow is 2806-2814, i.e. at the disk systemic velocity (narrow component, sigma 32), plus a broad blue-only skirt: centroid offset -125 km/s relative to the rotation-curve value (2769-2789); the skirt grows with distance from S (N-S centroid 2754 at -2.7", 2629 at -4.5", edge of emission ~-5.9"). (4) No blue tail at the mirror position N of S (blue half HCN 0.027+-0.006 vs 0.215+-0.010 Jy/beam km/s at Soutflow) nor at the W control, E control empty. (5) At 0.5" (Xb4b) the S-lobe pixel velocities scatter by 113 (HCO+)-262 (HCN) km/s rms with only a weak N-S gradient (+44+-5 / +27+-2 km/s/arcsec, r=0.15-0.21; E-W gradient -28..+15), i.e. clumps with up to ~100-250 km/s relative motions on <100 pc, not a smooth gradient (disk gradients here <~45 km/s/arcsec). Which predictions: a smooth warp/tidal arm predicts line widths set by the beam-smeared gradient (~60 km/s), velocities continuous with the E-W curve, and symmetric red/blue clumps; the data show one-sided broad blue gas with sigma 100-150 km/s, centroid shifted -100..-250 km/s and clump-to-clump scatter >100 km/s, which prefers an outflow/entrained or strongly perturbed gas. Not rejected: a tilted-ring warp with a PA twist and v_rot~250 km/s could project -100..-300 km/s on the minor axis, and a tidal feature. Classification stays MEDIUM: more consistent with the dense-gas blue lobe of the S outflow (position/direction match Sakamoto+2014 and Michiyama+2018) than an isolated cloud, but disk-warp/tidal origin is an unrejected alternative.
results.uncertainty: centroid +-10-20 km/s

results.value: Blue half (v_loc-400..-100) in the box (-1.7<dRA<1.3, -6.0<dDec<-3.3)": HCN 0.779+-0.030 Jy km/s, L'(3-2)=5.7e5 K km/s pc2; HCO+ 0.437+-0.015, L'(3-2)=3.1e5 (stat only). Route A (1-0 luminosity x alpha 3-10): M_dense(HCN) = 1.4e6-4.6e6 Msun, HCO+ 1.9e6-6.5e6. Route B (3-2 only, r31 between 0.3 and 1): HCN 1.7e6-1.9e7, HCO+ 0.9e6-1.0e7. Implied r31 (box 3-2 over M18 1-0) 1.2 (HCN), 0.5 (HCO+) with +-50% from differing apertures/windows and unknown M18 zero velocity, i.e. 3-2 and 1-0 together favour r31(HCN)>~0.6. Dense/CO fraction vs the CO high-velocity mass of the whole S outflow 2.5e7 X20 (Sakamoto+2014): route A 6-18% (X20=1) or 11-37% (alpha_CO halved, Pereira-Santaella+2024 X20=0.5); route B up to 76% / >100% (upper end unphysical). The CO mass covers both lobes and all velocities >~260 km/s while the HCN lobe is the blue half only, so these fractions are indicative within a factor ~2; the previous "20-25%" with alpha=10 and X20=1 is replaced by 6-37% (route A). alpha_HCN=10 (Gao & Solomon 2004, virialised cores) is likely an overestimate for outflowing gas; 3 is the low end used here.

results.quantity: Q3b: classification of the Soutflow candidate (summary after round 2)
results.value: Soutflow (1.9" = 370 pc S of S) is detected in HCN (12.6 sigma) and HCO+ (5 sigma) at the position of the blue lobe of the southern edge-on outflow (within 0.6" of Michiyama South-OF-Blue). Kinematics: one-sided broad (sigma 100-150 km/s) blue-shifted gas (-100..-400 km/s) on top of a narrow disk-like component at systemic velocity; no blue tail at mirror or E-W control positions; clump velocity scatter >100 km/s. Classification: dense-gas blue lobe of the S outflow, MEDIUM confidence; unrejected alternatives: tidal/warped disk gas. Chemistry: HCN/HCO+ 3-2 in the blue half 1.0-1.4 (fixed aperture; blend-corrected >=0.85-1.2), higher than S (0.46, >6 sigma), indistinguishable from N (1.13) and Bridge (1.3) in the same relative velocity bins; the broad component as a whole has 0.72-0.8; the "ratio 1.7-2" is a peak-selected, blue-tail value. No dense-gas wing at N above 3 sigma limits of 2-4% (HCN, 225-750 km/s blue) of the core flux. Dense mass of the lobe ~1.4-6.5e6 Msun (1-0 route). || REVISED after p0013/p0006-r01: Soutflow is a real one-lobe, one-sided HCN excess in the Xb4d outer blue window (6.2 sigma, uncleaned, 1.0 sigma in Xb4b); classification as a dense-gas outflow lobe is now LOW-MEDIUM confidence, and 'not a blend' is NOT established (HDO untestable). Blue-half ratio 1.0-1.4 is frame dependent; ratio >1 is not robust.
results.uncertainty: not quantified

results.quantity: Does the disk HCN/HCO+ decline reflect abundance or excitation? Forward-model constraint (proxy sky = 2-1 10" maps) and RADEX translation
results.value: Recovery alone (HCO+ 3-2 profile fixes the transfer function, f=0.075-0.275 of 8.7 m/lambda) would give R(8-12")/R(0-4")=0.80-0.84 for a 2-1-like truth, not the observed 0.44 (3-2). Fitting an extra intrinsic HCN fall eps in 3-2 gives eps=0.15 (1 sigma 0.10-0.20) Xb4f, 0.35 (0.25-0.40) Xb4d, i.e. total 0.05-0.45 allowed; flat (eps=0) excluded >2 sigma only for the assumed 8-12" sigma (0.06) and T(u) parametrisation. The 2-1 decline alone leaves intrinsic gradient unconstrained (eps 0-0.4). RADEX: a 15% lower R21 is only ~-0.07 dex in N(HCN)/N(HCO+) if thin; the stronger 3-2 fall needs lower HCN excitation (Tk 20-50 K, lower density) or up to ~0.5 dex lower HCN column, non-unique. Most plausible reading: excitation, not abundance (LOW confidence, model-dependent).
results.uncertainty: eps 0.05-0.45; model systematics (T(u) shape, PB width 22 vs 37", zero level, assumed sigma) not marginalised

results.quantity: Is the 1.05" N wing rise / ratio-vs-velocity slope a beam (spatial-mixing) effect? Matched-aperture, matched-beam, centroid and injection tests
results.value: Same aperture r<0.5" about N, 40-km/s bins over +-140 km/s, no mask: weighted linear slope Xb4d@1.05" +0.082+-0.006 per 100 km/s (chi2/dof const 221/6); Xb4b convolved to 1.05" +0.072+-0.008 (92/6) -> the two arrays agree (difference 1.0 sigma, so not an Xb4b-recovery effect); Xb4b at native-like 0.30" +-0.003+-0.013 (12/6, mean 0.875). Same data, same aperture, only the beam changes -> the slope is generated by the 1.05" beam. Injection (HCN = R(r_N)*HCO+ on the Xb4b HCO+ cube, R from the measured profile 0.98/0.82/0.63/0.48/0.40 at r=0.125/0.375/0.75/1.5/3", identical kinematics, smoothed to 1.05"): predicted slope +0.049 per 100 km/s (mean 0.78 vs observed 0.77): i.e. ~60-70% of the observed slope arises from a purely radial ratio gradient + velocity gradient, none from spectral variation; residual +0.02-0.03 per 100 km/s (3 sigma) is not reproduced (steeper unresolved central R(r) or genuine red-wing HCN excess). Centroids (HCN minus HCO+ per 40 km/s bin, r<1.2", Xb4d): dx = +0.04..+0.06" (blue), -0.001 (0), -0.09 (+80), -0.125+-0.034" (+120 km/s); Xb4b 0.30": +0.02 -> -0.038+-0.003" (+80); dy <=0.04": HCN emission is systematically closer to the nucleus than HCO+ at every velocity (HCO+ centroid moves -0.5" -> +0.28" across the line), with a larger offset on the red side, consistent with an HCN-richer compact core mixed in a 1.05" beam with lower-ratio extended gas
results.uncertainty: slopes +-0.006-0.013; centroid errors from S/N (0.6 FWHM/SNR) + no systematic astrometry; injection input R(r) measured at 0.30" so central gradient underestimated

results.quantity: 4-3/3-2 per molecule across the line profile at the common 6.5" beam, unmasked, window-integrated, and the N/S-weighted forward model (Xb47/Xb4f; weights from Xb4d 3-2 cubes at 6.5")
results.value: Unmasked Tb ratios: HCN -100..100 0.409+-0.003, -250..-100 0.40+-0.06, 100..250 0.386+-0.036; HCO+ -100..100 0.500+-0.002, -250..-100 0.504+-0.052, 100..250 0.396+-0.028 (red-wing drop 0.50 -> 0.40, 3.7 sigma). Per 40 km/s bin HCN 0.37-0.45 (core), HCO+ 0.44-0.52 (core), 0.353+-0.029 at +130. Xb4d->6.5" weights: the HCO+ 3-2 red wing (+100..250) is only 19% N / 81% S flux (core 56% N; HCN wing 52% N), blue wing 21% N. Fit I43=I32*(R_N f_N+R_S(1-f_N)) with constant R_N,R_S (bins with 3-2 S/N>3, |v|<=250): HCN R_N=0.459+-0.010, R_S=0.303+-0.020 (chi2/dof 63/10; single R 0.407, 90/11); HCO+ R_N=0.575+-0.008, R_S=0.402+-0.009 (127/8; single R 0.498, 231/9). The model predicts HCO+ red wing 0.434 (obs 0.396+-0.028; N/S weighting explains ~2/3 of the 0.50->0.40 drop, residual 0.04+-0.03 = 1.3 sigma) and HCN wing 0.384 (obs 0.386+-0.036). So the HCO+ red-wing drop is mostly N/S weighting (red HCO+ is S-dominated, S having lower 4-3/3-2: R_S/R_N=0.70 for HCO+, 0.66 for HCN), not an intrinsic velocity effect; the fits remain statistically poor (chi2/dof 6-16) because an extended component (Xb4d recovers only 78-80% of Xb4f 3-2 at |v|<100) and sub-structure in N and S are unmodelled; a third component with free ratio gave an unphysical R_E<0 (consistent with 0) and does not fix chi2
results.uncertainty: stat <=0.01 in cores, +-0.03-0.1 in wings; no flux-recovery correction (<~10% ladder systematic); model weights assume Xb4d recovers N/S compact flux fully

results.value: Native-like peak Tb (aperture mean r<0.25" at 0.30"): N HCN 1.5 K, HCO+ 1.6 K (peak pixel at 0.25": 2.63/2.82 K, Q4); S HCN 0.7 K, HCO+ 1.6 K (peak pixel 1.34/2.94 K). Per-channel Tb(HCN) = 0.972*Tb(HCO+) through the origin at N (0.30"), 0.428 at S, 0.778/0.379 at N/S at 1.05"; the per-channel ratio at N is 0.96 for channels above half peak, so lines do not saturate to different ceilings. RADEX grids (HCN, HCO+ LAMDA, H2, Tkin 20-300 K, n 1e3-1e8, N<=10^17.5 per 150 km/s, X=N(HCN)/N(HCO+) 0.3-10, equal filling, T_R>=observed Tb): N core ratio 0.99+-0.05 -> tau(HCN 3-2) 3-300 and tau(HCO+) 1-290 in >=95% of allowed models (X<=3.2), n>=1e6 cm-3, filling factor eta=Tb/T_R 0.02-0.35 (a 2.8 K peak against T_R of 8-150 K: strong beam dilution/clumping), 4-3/3-2 ladder 0.92 (thermalised) for both; i.e. ratio~1 is the equal-Tex optically-thick signature, independent of X for X<=3. S (0.42+-0.02): no model with both tau>3 and Tex within 10% gives 0.3-0.5 (0 of 541); allowed: HCN moderately thick (tau 0.3-30) with lower N(HCN)/N(HCO+)<=1 and n 1e5-1e8, or Tex(HCN)<Tex(HCO+) (sub-thermal, n~1e3.5-5.5 with X>=1 and ladder 0.28/0.43 -> matches the observed merged 0.41/0.50 only for that low-n branch). Wings: N 0.30" stacked 1.06+-0.13 is allowed by the same thick solutions as the core; the 1.05" wing value 1.20+-0.10 (Tb) is NOT reachable for X<=1 (R32 <=1.04 even at tau>>1) and needs X>=3 (HCN-enriched or HCO+ less opaque: tau(HCN) 0.7-3, tau(HCO+) 0.1-1.8 at X=3.2) or X=10 with tau(HCO+)~2 [Update: see Q3r4/Q4c entries for the J=1-0-informed branch masses.]
results.uncertainty: grid tolerance max(1 sigma,5%); RADEX unreliable for tau>1e3 (cut); X and filling degenerate with n,T

results.quantity: Q2: Test of the S low-n branch Tex(HCN)<Tex(HCO+) against the Q1 ladders, R32 and the published 1-0 ratio
results.value: S, both-thick classes, best model per Tex-ratio branch (Tex ratio<0.8 / 0.8-1.25 / >1.25): class A chi2 9.9 / 97 / 1584; class F2 (separate n) 7.9 / 38 / 762. In the low-Tex-ratio branch all ladder/R32/R10 pulls are within 1.7 sigma (HCN 3-2/2-1 pred 0.43 vs 0.33+-0.18, HCN 4-3/3-2 0.27 vs 0.27+-0.04, HCO+ 3-2/2-1 0.60 vs 0.40+-0.11, HCO+ 4-3/3-2 0.43 vs 0.44+-0.09, R32 0.40 vs 0.39, R10 0.61 vs 0.645); the equal-Tex branch reproduces the ladders (pulls <1.0 sigma) but fails R32 (8.3 sigma, pred 0.62) and R10 (3.7 sigma). So the ladders do not contradict the low-n/Tex(HCN)<Tex(HCO+) branch, and that branch is the only both-thick one that fits R32. It corresponds to X>~3 at T~30 K, n~10^4.5 (A) or n(HCN)>n(HCO+) (F2); X<=1 is allowed only with HCN tau<~10 (P(X<1)=0.30)
results.uncertainty: conditional on Tbg<=5 K: for Tbg 10/20 K the equal-Tex branch fits better (class A chi2 18.9/27.8 vs 27.7/127); ladder data have 14% cross-band scale + deblend spread (N/S ladder decomposition fits poorly at 6.5", chi2/dof 6-16, Q9)

results.quantity: Q2: Physical scales as functions of the ASSUMED X(HCN) and the CO surface-density constraint on X(HCN)
results.value: Per-cloud column N(HCN, dv=50)=N(dv=150)/3: log 15.5-16.0 (N, pooled 15.3-15.8; S 15.3-16.3). N(H2)=N(HCN)/X: X=1e-9 -> log N(H2) 24.3-24.8 (N) / 24.3-25.3 (S); X=1e-8 -> 23.3-23.8 / 23.3-24.3 (log Sigma_H2 3.6-4.1 N, 3.6-4.6 S Msun/pc2); X=1e-7 -> 22.3-22.8 / 22.3-23.3 (log Sigma 2.6-3.1, 2.6-3.6); path L=N(HCN)/(X n_H2) is a function of X (out/q2/q2_scales_cond.csv per class). Constraint form: if the HCN column fills the beam, N(H2)<=Sigma_max requires X(HCN) >= N(HCN)/(Sigma_max 4.6e19): for Sigma_max=470 (CO GMC median, Brunetti+2022) log X_min=-6.8 (N; 16-84% -7.1..-6.6), -6.3 (S; -7.1..-6.1) i.e. X>~1.5e-7 N, 5e-7 S; for 1e3 -> 7e-8 / 2e-7; 3e3 -> 2.4e-8 / 8e-8; 1e4 -> 7e-9 / 2e-8 (S pooled; per-class in csv). A Galactic-like X(HCN)~1e-8 is compatible only if the nuclear Sigma_H2 >~1e4 Msun/pc2 or if the HCN-emitting source fills <<1 of the beam / the thick-line column is overestimated (n,N degenerate). NOT a finding: any statement about the dense-gas volume filling fraction (L/2R depends on the assumed X and the CO Sigma/R; the earlier 'fills <1-3% of the cloud' is withdrawn)
results.uncertainty: X(HCN) is assumed (1e-9..1e-7), not measured; Sigma_max is a literature GMC value (not NGC 3256 nuclear CO at 0.3"); 1 Msun/pc2=4.6e19 H2 cm-2 incl. He; filling 1; classes A,B,F2 shown separately in the csv, pooled equal weight

results.value: YES for the lobe, NO for the nuclear wings. Observed lobe wing (-405..-150 km/s) HCO+ 0.31, HCN 0.30 Jy km/s (Xb4b) vs beam-smeared-rotation null prediction <=0.008 / <=0.005. results.quantity: Q12c (HEADLINE): does a compact-core + envelope two-component non-LTE model fix the N one-zone fit and change the S result; is the N-vs-S temperature contrast significant?
results.value: No second component is required, and none is excluded. (1) With 7 independent data the one-zone N fit is marginal only if the beam geometry is held fixed (profile chi2 9.1/3 dof, p=0.028); with the geometry (extended filling at 1.7", compact size) given the widths measured from the 0.25/0.95/1.7/5.7" Tb growth curve it is acceptable (chi2 3.2/3, p=0.36; 1.5-3.2, p=0.36-0.67 over the measured-geometry variants). (2) The Bayesian preference for two components at N (dlnZ(2cT-1z)=+3.0, fixed geometry) vanishes with measured geometry (-1.7), with the 25% error floor (+1.2) and with judgement geometry widths (-0.2 to +0.7); in simulations the +3 threshold is exceeded by 14.5% [10-20%] of data-consistent one-zone truths with wrong sizes, so it is not significant; with measured-geometry priors the statistic has no power to separate the truths (two-comp truths give dlnZ -1.0 to -1.2, one-zone truths -0.4 to -2.1). (3) S: one-zone adequate (chi2 5.2/3, p=0.16; measured geometry 3.1/3), dlnZ -0.8 to +0.4; Tkin 19-23 K (16-84% 14-35 K), Tbg<=5 K branch unchanged (20 K [14,32] at Tbg 5 K), P(T>=80 K)<=0.06. N compact Tkin is unconstrained (12-96 K; 62 [39,96] fixed-geometry one-zone, 15 [12,25] measured-geometry one-zone, 27 [14,70] two-comp). (4) Delta T = T_N - T_S is unconstrained: joint draw-by-draw over 16 deblend variants P(T_N>T_S)=0.47-0.60 with measured geometry (variant range 0.23-0.88), 0.72-0.93 at fixed geometry; Delta T median -0.5..+4 K [16-84%: -10, +36] with measured geometry, +10..+35 K at fixed geometry. (5) H13CN 4-3 removes 50-80% of the N two-comp posterior mass (survival 0.20-0.50) and S 20-30%; compact tau32 median 23-37 -> 5-14 at N; the strongest earlier claim (n_c>1e6, tau32 10-100) is not robust.

results.value: One-zone (profile chi2 at best fit incl. g,h nuisance penalties; dof = 7 data - 4 effective params): N fixed geometry 9.13/3 (p=0.028, AIC 17.1, BIC 16.9); 25% floor 3.9/3 (p=0.27); Tbg 5 K 9.6/3 (p=0.02); measured geometry 3.2/3 (p=0.36), +30% size 1.5/3 (p=0.67); with 'us' judgement widths 2.8/3 (p=0.43). Two-component models have 8 (shared T) or 9 (independent T) effective parameters for 7 data: dof=-1/-2, chi2~0 and AIC 16.0/18.0, BIC 15.6/17.5 vs one-zone 17.1/16.9 (N) are parameter counting only; adding Tint and the extended excess (r7a/r7full, 9-11 data, same maps, double counted) gives one-zone N chi2 11.2/4 (p=0.02) fixed, 4.4/4 (p=0.36) measured geometry. results.quantity: Q12c: calibration of the evidence statistic: false-positive rate and power of dlnZ>=3 (200 simulated N data sets per truth, including mis-specified geometry)
results.value: Fit with fixed geometry ('base'): P(dlnZ>=3) = 0/200 (95% upper bound 1.8%) if the truth is the one-zone best fit with the assumed geometry; 29/200 = 14.5% (9.9-20.2%) if the truth is a one-zone model with 2-1 compact size x1.35 and 4-3 x0.74 that still fits the observed N data (chi2 4.4/3); 0/200 for the opposite shift (x0.74/x1.35: not data-consistent, chi2 28.5). Power: 54.5% (two-component truth, same geometry), 33% (two-comp, u=2, refit to data), 52% (u=0.5). The observed +3.02 is exceeded in 14.5% of the data-consistent geometry-mis-specified one-zone simulations (p=0.145; 0.00 for the correctly specified one). With the measured-geometry priors the statistic is negative for all truths (median over simulations: one-zone truths -2.1 to +0.1, two-comp truths u=2/0.5: -1.0/-1.2; P(dlnZ>=3)=0/200 for every truth) and the observed -1.67 lies at P(dlnZ>=obs)=0.37-0.97, i.e. the data have no power to separate one from two components once geometry is free (the dlnZ distributions of the two-component and one-zone truths overlap). Chi2 of the one-zone fit: P(chi2>=9.1)=0.015 (right geometry), 0.30 (mis-specified geometry), 0.49-0.68 (two-component truths).

results.value: Unconstrained. Joint fit (N and S fitted with the SAME deblend variant, 16 variants, mixture of posteriors; N-S ladder correlations across variants 0.15-0.65): measured geometry two-comp: Delta T = +3.7 K (16-84% -10, +36), P(T_N>T_S)=0.60 (per-variant 0.42-0.81); with H13CN +5.9 [-10,+55], 0.62 (0.45-0.95); one-zone measured geometry -0.5 [-11,+8], 0.47 (0.23-0.88). Independent-posterior calculation with Gaussian copula rho=-0.5/0/+0.5: P(T_N>T_S) = 0.58/0.60/0.64 (measured, two-comp), 0.66/0.69/0.75 (fixed), so the deblend covariance moves P by <=0.1. The 2-1/3-2/4-3 beams (9x6, 5.7x3.5, 4.3x2.8") are matched only through the model dilution term (4.47" round beam for all lines); the cross-weight of N and S at 10" is 0.48 (team-b s63). N and S temperatures are not distinguishable; what is robust is that HCN/HCO+ differs, not T.

results.value: 1-0 HCN/HCO+ 0.61+-0.25 (1.5", X145), 0.59+-0.11 (2.2", X961) vs 3-2 1.39+-0.16 (1.5"), 1.24+-0.16 (2.2"): the high 3-2 lobe ratio does NOT persist in 1-0 (difference 2.6 sigma at 1.5", 3.3 sigma at 2.2", statistical only). 1.5" lobe: HCN 1-0 2.3+-0.8, HCO+ 1-0 3.8+-0.8 K km/s; 3-2 HCN 1.1, HCO+ 0.8 -> r31(HCN) 0.50+-0.18, r31(HCO+) 0.22+-0.05 (S nucleus 0.22 / 0.34): HCN 3-2 is relatively strong in the lobe, i.e. HCO+ 3-2 is weak (r31(HCO+) is the lowest of any region) and HCN r31 is the highest, but only at 2.8 sigma. The 1-0 lobe ratio equals the S-nucleus value (0.57-0.58): at 1.5-2.2" the lobe window (-320..-180) is contaminated by the blue wing of the S nucleus 1.85" away, so the 1-0 ratio cannot be distinguished from S-nucleus leakage, while the 3-2 ratio (1.2-1.4) differs from the S nucleus 3-2 (0.38) by 5 sigma even at 2.2". Weak lines: SiO, HC3N, HNC, H13CO+, H13CN, HN13C all undetected (3 sigma limits 0.6-0.8 K km/s; HNC/HCN<0.5, SiO/HCO+<0.36, uninformative). Literature: Michiyama+2018 (ApJ 868, 95; full text retrieved via lit.py) report HCO+(1-0)/CO(1-0)=0.20+-0.04 in the S outflow vs 0.08+-0.01 in the S nucleus (dense-gas fraction higher in the outflow) and R32/10(CO)=1.3+-0.2 vs 0.7; I could not retrieve a numerical HCN/HCO+ 1-0 value for the S outflow from the extracted text, so the claim of a high 1-0 HCN/HCO+ in the S outflow is not verified here. Our 1-0 ratio (0.6+-0.1-0.25) is not high; Harada+2018 give only per-nucleus values (N 0.96, S 0.645 at 1.7"). [CAVEAT p0036: the 3-2 lobe ratios here use the Xb4d 12-m image; the 12-m flux loss (up to +34% at S in HCN) was not re-measured for the lobe, so the 2.6-3.3 sigma 1-0 vs 3-2 lobe difference is not re-tested with uv-complete 3-2 and stays low confidence.]

results.value: Posteriors essentially unchanged from the Xb4d-based fit: N Tk 22-40 K (broad 11-158), log n 3.9-4.0, log A=N(HCN)/N(HCO+) 0.70 (A~5); S Tk 112-141 K (35-251), log n 4.0, log A 0.40 (A~2.5); Bridge Tk 80-112 K, log A 0.5-0.6. ln BF N vs S (vs free fit), 1-0+3-2, 2.2": same Tk,n with free columns (abundance-only) +1.02; same A, free Tk,n (excitation-only) +0.21; same A and N (excitation+column) +1.31 (old: +1.30, -0.04, +0.97); 1.5": +0.26, -0.42, -0.10. Model-free: D=1.00+-0.04 and r31 N/S=1.0 mean nothing requires different excitation; the N/S difference is in the HCN/HCO+ ratio at both J, i.e. an abundance (or opacity/column) signal. The lower N Tk and ~2x higher N HCN/HCO+ column ratio are driven by the 1-0 ratio and weakly by line opacity.

results.quantity: Q10 (answer): the N inward rise of HCN/HCO+ 3-2 is a property of the N nucleus, not a function of continuum surface brightness: it saturates at the thick/thermalised value R~1 at the core, follows the dust continuum only within N, and S stays flat although its 1.1 mm continuum is 40-65% free-free/synchrotron
results.value: (1) N: R=0.98/0.87/0.45/0.30 for r=0-0.15/0.25-0.5/1-1.5/2-3" (0.30" beam), 0.805/0.726/0.599/0.474/0.399 at 1.05"; S: R=0.42/0.41/0.40/0.36/0.33 (0.30"), 0.39/0.36/0.36/0.39 (1.05") while its continuum falls 100x. (2) Pooled N+S pixels: once a nucleus indicator is included, R has no significant dependence on log continuum, log HCO+ or radius (0.30": std. coeff on log Sc +0.05 [+0.02,+0.09] against a shifted-continuum null of 0.00+-0.05; nucleus term -0.14 [-0.19,-0.08]; 1.05": log Sc +0.01 [-0.05,+0.06], nucleus -0.18 [-0.22,-0.13], R^2 0.70 vs 0.32 without it). At equal HCO+ brightness N and S differ (0.40-0.80 Jy/b km/s: R=0.63+-0.04 vs 0.43+-0.04; 0.30"). (3) Within N alone R rises with continuum at 0.30" (std. slope +0.08 [+0.06,+0.10], null -0.01+-0.04; partially degenerate with radius), S alone: none. (4) Velocity-resolved R is flat across the line (N 1.01+-0.03/1.01+-0.01/0.97+-0.02 blue/core/red; S 0.43+-0.01/0.39+-0.02/0.36+-0.05): no self-absorption/opacity or wing signature. (5) RADEX: R from 0.4 to 1.0 at fixed 4-3/3-2 ladders needs X=N(HCN)/N(HCO+) up by x3-4 (log X +0.5-0.6) -- or an HCO+ deficit of the same size; density (>=2 dex) or column (>=1 dex) changes cannot do it without raising the HCN 4-3/3-2 ratio to 0.8-0.9 (observed 0.39 N, 0.27 S). R~1 at N core is the thermalised/thick ceiling.
results.uncertainty: see sub-entries Q10a-Q10h

results.quantity: Q10g: RADEX consequences (LAMDA, Tbg 2.73 K, dv 150 km/s): what each interpretation predicts for R vs continuum and for the ladders
results.target: N and S, grid Tk 20-150 K, log n 3-7, N(HCO+) 1e14-1e17, X 0.3-30
results.value: R32 (Tb ratio) saturates at ~1 for thick, thermalised gas (e.g. Tk=30, N(HCO+)=1e16.5, n>=1e6: R=0.82-1.0 even for X=3), so the N core R=0.93-1.0 sits at the ceiling; it cannot rise further with continuum. Reference S-like state (Tk 30-80, log n=4, N(HCO+)=1e16, X=3): R=0.29-0.40. Single-parameter moves to R~1.0: (i) abundance ratio X x3-4 (X 3->10): R=0.97-1.22 with 4-3/3-2 unchanged (HCN 0.23-0.39, HCO+ 0.35-0.47) -- matches the observed similar N/S ladders (HCN 0.39/0.27, HCO+ 0.48/0.44); (ii) density 1e4->1e6.5: R=0.4->0.8-1.0 but HCN 4-3/3-2 -> 0.78-0.9 (excluded by 0.39); (iii) column N(HCO+) 1e16->1e17: R only 0.29->0.43 (Tk=30), 0.40->0.52 (80 K); (iv) IR pumping/Tbg: dust Tb at 355 GHz 0.3 (N)/1.0 K (S) -> Tbg,eff 3.0/3.7 K, R changes <few %, v2=1f <3-6%. => abundance (X(HCN)/X(HCO+) up by ~0.5-0.6 dex, equivalently HCO+ depleted/destroyed in N) is the only single change that explains R without changing ladders; HCN and HCO+ individually: HCO+ ∝ continuum, HCN concentrates (Q10a). With CS 7-6/HCO+ N/S = 2.1+-0.3 but CS/HCN 1.1+-0.2 (Q14e, 4-6" beams) N is HCO+-poor rather than HCN-rich relative to S. Not discriminated: starburst chemistry (mechanical heating/cosmic rays: would make R follow SFR density, which is not seen across nuclei), XDR/AGN (S has the AGN, but lowest R, so an X-ray/AGN-driven HCN enhancement is disfavoured at S); HCO+ destruction by higher electron fraction/lower ionisation in the dense N core is allowed.
results.uncertainty: grid steps 0.5 dex in n, 1 dex in N; ladders from Q1b

results.quantity: Q35: is the N-vs-S CS excitation contrast the cause of the J-dependent sign (HCN-rich vs HCO+-poor)? CS ladder 2-1/5-4/7-6 and thin-tracer excitation at N, S, Bridge
results.value: CS 5-4/2-1 (K km/s, 1.7") N 0.315, S 0.202, C 0.180 -> N/S = 1.57 [1.28,1.94]; for comparison HCN 3-2/1-0 N/S 1.16 [1.00,1.34], HCO+ 3-2/1-0 N/S 0.90 [0.78,1.03] (r31 of HCN and HCO+ equal at N and S, Q34), and the thin tracers C18O 2-1/1-0 N/S 1.48 [1.25,1.74], 13CO 2-1/1-0 1.34 [1.16,1.54]. So the excitation enhancement at N is shared by CS and by the CO isotopologues (lower-density gas) and is absent in HCN and HCO+ 3-2/1-0: it is a property of the gas, not a CS peculiarity. Joint RADEX fit (common Tk, n, eta for HCN, HCO+, CS; Harada six lines + CS7-6/HCN4-3 and HCN4-3/HCO+4-3 at 4.3"): N Tk 199 [178,223] K, log n 4.50 [4.38,4.62]; S Tk 100 [63,158] K, log n 4.62 [4.38,4.88]; Bridge(C) Tk 178 [141,223], log n 4.25 [4.12,4.50]. The HCN+HCO+-only fit gives N Tk 22 [11,141], S 50 [20,112] (degenerate). CS Tex(2-1/5-4/7-6) N 11/9/17 K, S 13/8/14 K, Bridge 7/9/17 K: all strongly sub-thermal (n_crit(5-4)~1e6), Tex contrast N/S <~1.1 at 5-4 and ~1.2 at 7-6, i.e. the CS contrast is a Tk (and tau) contrast, not a Tex contrast. Test: predicted CS 5-4/2-1 from the HCN+HCO+ (Tk,n) with N(CS)/N(HCN)=0.03-1 is 0.10 [0.04,0.23] at N (observed 0.315, 1.2-3x above), 0.10 [0.05,0.22] at S (observed 0.20, consistent), 0.08 [0.05,0.13] at C (0.18). The CS ladder is hotter than HCN/HCO+ only at N (and weakly at C); best-fit chi2 of the one-gas ladder at N is 10.2 for ~0 dof (11.6 for dof 2 with the 4.3" ratios) vs 2.1/3.5 at S: a single-gas model is disfavoured at N, so the CS normalisation at N carries an excitation systematic. Consequence for the sign flip: HCO+/CS N/S 1.09 (1-0/2-1) -> 0.63 (3-2/5-4) -> 0.68 (4-3/7-6) is the CS(low J) vs CS(high J) change, at constant HCN/HCO+ (1.49, 1.92, 1.62). Absolute RADEX N(CS) is not tied to a single excitation (Tex 8-17 K) so the J=2-1 and 5-4/7-6 CS-normalised results are two different corrections of the same N-S contrast; after the joint fit the column-density ratios (next entry) are the J-free answer. RADEX check of the 4-3/3-2 hot-gas C18O 2-1/1-0 prediction (3.7-4.0 at Tk 100-200 K, n=3e4) is far above the observed 1.1-1.6 (C18O comes from lower density gas than HCN/HCO+), so the thin CO ratio is used only for the sign of the N-S contrast.

results.quantity: Q35: column-density ratios N(HCN)/N(HCO+), N(CS)/N(HCN), N(CS)/N(HCO+) at N, S, Bridge and their N/S contrasts (excitation-corrected): which species departs?
results.value: Adopted fit (6 lines at 1.7" + 2 ratios at 4.3"), medians [16-84%]: log N(HCN)/N(HCO+) N 0.6, S 0.4, C 0.4 (+-0.1 grid); N(CS)/N(HCN) ~0.25 [-0.6 dex, +-0.1] at all three; N(CS)/N(HCO+) 1.0 N, 0.63 S, 0.63 C. N/S contrasts: N(HCN)/N(HCO+) = 1.64 [1.31,2.09] (P>1 = 1.00); N(CS)/N(HCN) = 0.96 [0.71,1.28] (P>1=0.45); N(CS)/N(HCO+) = 1.58 [1.19,2.12] (P>1 = 0.94); i.e. N(HCN)/N(CS) = 1.04 [0.78,1.41] and N(HCO+)/N(CS) = 0.63 [0.47,0.84] (P>1 = 0.06). Bridge/S: N(HCN)/N(HCO+) 1.03 [0.83,1.32], N(CS)/N(HCN) 1.07 [0.76,1.54], N(CS)/N(HCO+) 1.11 [0.79,1.62]. Without the 4.3" ratios: N(HCN)/N(HCO+) N/S 1.65 [1.33,2.19], N(HCO+)/N(CS) N/S 0.62 [0.44,0.83]; HCN+HCO+ only: N(HCN)/N(HCO+) N/S 2.40 [1.71,3.25]. ANSWER: with CS as the reference, HCN tracks CS (N/S 1.0) and it is HCO+ whose column is lower at N by ~0.6 (2.5 sigma on the posterior; P(N/S>1)=0.06), i.e. N is HCO+-poor, not HCN-rich, in this normalisation. This conclusion rests on CS being a faithful abundance reference at N; the one-gas model fits the CS ladder less well at N (chi2 10 vs 2 at S), and a different reference (C18O 1-0, CS 2-1) gives HCN-rich (N/S 1.5-1.6) and HCO+ flat (1.0-1.1); see the normaliser entry. Thin limit, no 4-3 detection assumed: H13CN/H13CO+ 1-0 (2.2", Q29) = 0.75 [0.60,0.93] N, 0.23 [0.09,0.42] S (1 sigma, truncated >=0; 3-sigma upper 1.15), 0.94 [0.72,1.22] Bridge; N/S = 3.3 [1.7,9.0], P(N/S>1) = 0.97, 5th percentile 1.19 (S is only a 1-sigma H13CN value: weak evidence, ~2 sigma, not used in the conclusion). With a RADEX conversion N(H13CN)/N(H13CO+) = 2.9 (x/divide 1.25) x intensity ratio (Q29 s188, n=1e4-1e5) and a common 12C/13C of 30-100 (cancels): N(HCN)/N(HCO+) = 2.2 [1.6,3.0] N, 0.65 [0.24,1.3] S, 2.7 [1.9,3.9] Bridge; N/S of the column ratio 3.6 [1.3,11.8] with 0.15 dex independent isotopic-fractionation factors per species (P>1 = 0.90). This agrees with the optically-thick-corrected 12-line ratio N/S 1.6 within errors but cannot discriminate (H13CN at S is undetected). Harada+2018 give no HCN/HCO+ abundances for NGC 3256 (Table 13 is line intensities; HCN/HCO+ 1-0 = 0.96 N, 0.65 S, 0.67 C), so the comparison is with their line ratios only (reproduced).

interpretation:
Community answer. The data resolve the two nuclei, the Bridge, compact clumps and one southern blue-shifted component, but not a defensible disk; they give limits on density/temperature (Tk > ~56 K, n < ~10^5.25 cm-3 at 10") and show N-vs-S excitation differences are untestable at 10".
(1) Nuclei. N and S are separable at Bands 6 and 7 (0.25-4"), not in Band 5. At a matched 1.05" beam HCN/HCO+ 3-2 is 0.83+-0.04 at N and 0.40+-0.02 at S (N/S 2.0-2.1), constant over the line core, insensitive to velocity window (<=2.5%), array (Xb4b vs Xb4d) and missing flux (<=9% across Band 6 arrays despite 47-65% recovery of extended HCO+); two teams agree. The AGN nucleus therefore has the LOWEST ratio, i.e. no HCN enhancement at the AGN, as Harada+2018 found with Band 3 data; this is a prediction-test of the HCN/HCO+ AGN diagnostic that fails here. The contrast is lost at coarse beams (1.2 at 6.5", 1.07 at 10") because N and S blend and N's compact HCN-rich core is diluted, which is why unmatched native-beam ratios (N 0.5-1.0) misled; deblending recovers N/S ~1.9+-0.5 at 4-3 (N 0.47, S 0.25) and is unconstrained at 2-1.
(2) Excitation and origin. The 10" ladders (3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2: HCN ~0.37/0.31, HCO+ ~0.49/0.42) are strongly sub-thermal and identical at N, S and Bridge, but that is because the 10" apertures overlap (N-S 5.1", weight 0.48): N vs S excitation is NOT testable at 10" (intrinsic core contrast <~2 allowed, >=4 needed for detection). Single-zone RADEX on the 10" ladder gives only limits: Tk > ~56 K (84%) with no upper bound and n(H2) < ~10^5.25 cm-3 (P/k ~10^6.6), with a compact/clumpy emitting area (eta~0.02, ~330 pc) and N(H2) uncertain by ~1 dex per assumed abundance; cold (<30 K) and very dense (>1e6) single zones are excluded. The 1.7" J=1-0 data (Harada+2018, Michiyama+2018, literature assumptions) show that the N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast is already 1.49 at 1-0 versus ~2.0 at 3-2, so ~60% of it (in log) is J-independent and at most ~40% excitation. Adding the 1-0 datum, thin-HCN/abundance-only explanations are disfavoured at S (thin mass 0.26 -> 0.04-0.06; team-a delta chi2>=28-64) and filling-only fails the 1-0 prediction; both lines are probably optically thick (HCN tau32 > ~2, no upper limit), with a 1.8-3x lower HCN column (opacity or abundance) at S (A_N/A_S~3 in team-b's compact fit) rather than a density or temperature difference. At N the 1-0 datum is not decisive, and the N core (R 0.97 at r<0.25", 0.4 at 2-3"; S flat at ~0.4) can be saturated lines or thin lines with a ~3x higher HCN/HCO+ abundance ratio. CS and the low-J literature (HCO+ tracks CS, HCN and HNC lower at S) weakly favour an HCN deficit at S over HCO+ enhancement (CS 7-6 alone 1.2 sigma, undecided). H13CN is undetected (HCN/H13CN > 8.3 at N) and, with predicted HCN/H13CN 17-68, cannot test opacity at the present depth; the earlier 'tau<3.8-12.8' bounds hold only for equal Tex. IR pumping is limited to Tvib < 290-430 K (CON-like 200-300 K not excluded); HCO+ continuum absorption (0.2-0.6 K) is not needed. All RADEX statements are one-zone, 1-4 dof and prior-dependent (low-medium confidence); the only significant between-region excitation difference at 10" is the cooler E1 disk position (Tk <~56 K, P=0.94, HCN-driven; depends on common calibration and the E1 HCN 4-3 PB/recovery systematic).
(3) Outflow. Both teams find a real elongated (~2", ~0.4 kpc) blue-shifted dense-gas structure attached to the S nucleus (HCN 12.6 sigma, HCO+ ~5 sigma; not a sidelobe; no blue tail at the mirror or E-W control positions; no red gas beyond the S disk red edge). Kinematics (team-a p0006): narrow disk-like component at systemic velocity (sigma 32 km/s, HCN/HCO+ 0.35, as S) plus a one-sided broad (sigma 100-150 km/s) blue skirt growing with distance from S, line widths not explained by beam-smeared rotation; position and sense match the blue CO(3-2) lobe of Sakamoto+2014 and Michiyama+2018 South-OF-Blue (0.56" away), with a red wing 3.5" north of S. We classify it as a candidate dense-gas blue lobe of the S outflow with LOW-MEDIUM confidence; a warped/tidal disk feature is not rejected. REVISED after team-b (p0013, p0006-r01): the HCN-over-HCO+ excess in the outer blue window (-405..-205 km/s) at 1.8" S of S is a real, one-sided, artefact-free feature in Xb4d (0.262+-0.042 Jy/b km/s, 6.2 sigma; R_outer 1.9+-0.4 vs core 0.54) but only 1.0 sigma in Xb4b (2 sigma below Xb4d), it is uncleaned flux, and its nature (HCN-rich wing gas vs a lobe-confined blend such as HDO, which cannot be tested) is undecided, so 'not a blend' is not established. The blue-half ratio is frame dependent (1.0-1.4; 1.2+-0.2 is a central value, not R>1 robustly; the earlier 1.7-1.8 was peak-selected and is dropped; whole broad component 0.72-0.8). The wing ratio exceeds the S core robustly (0.4-0.6; >6 sigma) but is NOT distinguishable from the blue-side ratios of N (1.13) and the Bridge (1.32) in the same relative-velocity bins: the rise of HCN/HCO+ toward the blue is common to several positions, so it is not specific to the AGN-hosting S outflow, and R_wing>1 is not robust across arrays. The HCN excess is not explained by blends of CH3NH2, CH3OH, CH2NH, CH3CHO, CH3SH, c-C3H or l-C3H (bounds <=1-18%), but HDO is untestable. Comparison with Nishimura+2024 (high HCN/HCO+ in outflows from shock chemistry) is therefore only suggestive; Harada+2018's 'no enhancement at the AGN' holds for the nucleus. The N nucleus has no dense wing (HCN 225-750 km/s: <2-4% of core, 3 sigma), consistent with Michiyama+2018's non-detection of a northern dense outflow (pole-on gas extended >2" unconstrained). Dense mass of the lobe ~1.4-6.5e6 Msun (1-0 route, alpha 3-10; low confidence), i.e. ~6-37% of the S high-velocity CO mass; r31(HCN)~0.6, ~2x HCO+. Fluxes are lower limits (clean mask), and no one has compared with CO kinematics directly. RADEX for the lobe is under-constrained (no dof).
(4) Chemistry. CH3OH is detected (Band 5 Q-branch; 254.015 GHz) and cold if LTE (Trot S 13 (10-20) K with the p0020 empirical-ramp blend, Bridge ~30 K with a lower bound ~17 K, N unconstrained; blend integral N 1.13, S 1.61, Bridge 1.69, W 0.72 Jy/b km/s at +-14-37%, after identifying the spw22 edge ramp as a continuum-proportional processing residual; ~9 K is not a constraint, the Q-branch 'excess' is baseline-driven and withdrawn). The 254 GHz line suggests a Bridge/W enhancement at 1-4" (CH3OH/HCO+ ~0.04-0.07 vs <0.02 at nuclei, 3-4 sigma, one transition: tentative), but at the 9" Band-5 beam the ratio is 0.05 everywhere (no contrast, errors 40-80%). Qualitatively similar to, agreeing with Harada+2018 and Michiyama+2020 (shock/low-excitation tracer off the nuclei); extended emission is only mildly resolved out (0.7-0.8 recovery after matched smoothing). SO 5(4)-4(3) in Band 5 and CS 7-6 are detected; HOC+ is tentative; SO 6_5-5_4 is not covered; the Band 6 SO feature is a limit.
(5) Disk. Only Band 5 HCO+/HCN 2-1 at r=8-12" gives a disk ratio, now measured by both teams (0.47-0.50, i.e. 10-25% below 0.55-0.62 at r<8"; zero-level systematic up to +-0.1); beyond 12" and in Bands 6/7 it fails go/no-go; its 3-2 deficit is degenerate between missing short spacings (a 13-14" structure with an 8.7 m uv hole reproduces the HCO+ deficit with nuclear excitation) and low excitation, and HCN 3-2 depends on the zero level by a factor ~4. Hence resolution and sensitivity force an 'active region versus extended gas' comparison at J=2-1 and for the disk, but nuclei, Bridge and the southern component are separable at J=3-2 and 4-3.
(6) Not done: cloud sizes/linewidths versus Brunetti+2021,2022, outflow-CO comparison, non-LTE of CH3OH beyond formal fits. Continuum alpha(B5-B7)~1.5 with up to half of the Band 6 flux resolved out.
(7) Array systematics (p0008). Nested recovery at the centre is Xb4d/Xb4f ~0.7 (HCO+ and HCN, and Band 6 continuum 0.68-0.73), so the 12-m arrays lose 30-40% relative to the ACA but equally in both lines; matched-J HCN/HCO+ is safe (true/observed Xb4f ratio N 1.03, S 1.08, Bridge 1.04 under differential-loss sensitivity). Ladder ratios across Xb55/Xb4f/Xb47 carry a <~10% prior-dominated recovery systematic, below calibration error, so the 'no N/S ladder difference' statement is unaffected. After removing nuclear contamination the E1 clump is compact and nuclear-like; W is extended and resolved out, so disk statements at 3-2/4-3 rest on the ACA alone and the apparent disk T21/T32 excess at E1/E2 disappears.

UPDATE (p0005-r02): team-a independently reproduced the inward rise of N HCN/HCO+ (0.98 inner 0.15" to ~0.4 at 1.5-3"), flat S (~0.4), and the 2-1 disk annuli, and showed via smoothing to a common beam and flat-ratio injection that the gradient is not an array/pipeline artefact. The HCN-rich region at N is resolved at ~0.3-1" (60-200 pc), more extended than the ratio~1 core (<0.25"). As before, the ratios do not separate abundance from opacity/excitation, and the absence of an enhancement at the AGN-hosting S nucleus is consistent with Harada et al. 2018.

(8) Velocity dependence of HCN/HCO+ (p0010, p0005-r03; supersedes earlier wing readings). At 0.30" the N ratio is 0.92-1.04 over +-100 km/s (about 12% blue-to-red decline) and 1.05+-0.13 at 100-260 km/s: no significant wing rise. The ~1.2 wing ratio seen at 1.05" (core 0.77) is largely beam mixing: the same Xb4b data give slope -0.003+-0.013 per 100 km/s at 0.30" and +0.072+-0.008 after convolution to 1.05"; injecting the measured radial profile reproduces 60-70% of it (0.02-0.03 per 100 km/s unexplained; HCN centroid lies 0.04-0.13" nearer N than HCO+). Hence wing 'excesses' at N, Bridge and the Soutflow blob from ~1" data should not be read as intrinsic. The S deficit (0.375-0.44) persists at all velocities where HCN is detected (to ~260 km/s), favouring an abundance/excitation difference over a core-only opacity effect; the Bridge wing ratio (1.35+-0.32) is only 2.9 sigma. The 6.5" HCO+ 4-3/3-2 red-wing drop (0.50 to 0.40) is mostly N/S weighting. Opacity vs abundance remains undecided (equal-Tex thick lines at N, S needs lower HCN abundance or Tex).

(9) Q2 non-LTE ranges, floor-free (team-a p0012, confirmed compatible with team-b p0011 by p0011-r01). At 1" matched beams (N-S separated), one-zone RADEX with optically thick, sub-thermal HCN and HCO+ gives log n(H2) 4.5-5.5 at both nuclei (not distinguishable, agreeing with team-b's n<10^5.25 at 10"), N Tkin ~25-100 K (pooled median 80 K, poorly fit, chi2 19-23/8, class dependent) and S Tkin ~15-50 K (median 25 K, >=80 K excluded at >3 sigma; T>~19 K one-sided 95%). The earlier S 30-40 K was an artefact of a 30 K prior floor and is withdrawn. Team-b's 10" centre Tk>~56 K is dominated by the warm N and is consistent. The 'warm N, cool S' contrast is only suggestive (N class B fits at 29 K; allowed ranges overlap at 25-50 K); the robust difference is the excitation pattern Tex(HCN)/Tex(HCO+) 0.86 (N) vs 0.63 (S), valid only for Tbg<=5 K (continuum-based Tbg,eff 3.0-3.7 K; for Tbg>=10 K the S equal-Tex branch wins). Bridge, disk, wings and the S outflow lobe have one or two ratios only: n>=1e5 cm-3 from R32, no temperature constraint. X(HCN) is not measured; with a beam-filling HCN column the CO surface density needs X(HCN)>~1e-7 (Sigma 470 Msun/pc2) to >~1e-8 (Sigma 1e4); the earlier 'fills <1-3% of the cloud' statement is withdrawn. H13CN and CS add no constraint on the solutions.

(10) Wing ratios, round 3 (team-b p0013 with p0005-r04, p0006-r01, p0009-r02, p0010-r01; all CONFIRM team-a within errors except the Soutflow nature). (i) At N the wing/core HCN/HCO+ ratio is 1.00+-0.14 at 0.25" and 1.21-1.41 at 1.05": the wing rise is beam mixing (confirmed by two teams; team-b revised its own earlier p0005 wing result). (ii) The S deficit (0.4-0.6) persists at all velocities, within 1.5 sigma, with the Xb4d blue outer lobe the one exception. (iii) The S-outflow HCN excess is a one-array, one-lobe feature of undecided nature. (iv) N has no dense wing above ~3% of the core (baseline-limited; consistent with Michiyama+2018). Net: no velocity-resolved evidence that the dense-gas HCN/HCO+ ratio is intrinsically enhanced in wings at either nucleus; the S lobe is a candidate worth higher-sensitivity, HDO-sensitive follow-up.

(Update, p0014.) The southern blue dense-gas lobe (~365 pc S of S) is not produced by beam-smeared rotation (null prediction <=0.01 vs 0.30 Jy km/s observed), and its position and geometry match the CO outflow (plane-of-sky, i~70-80 deg); the nuclear wings do not separate from rotation. A real one-sided red ridge also sits between S and N. Its dense mass is ~1e7 Msun (x3-10, abundance dominated, comparable to or below the CO outflow mass) and the dense Mdot ~10-60 Msun/yr (1.5 dex, geometry dominated). Whether the lobe's HCN excess (outer-window ratio 1.9+-0.4 in Xb4d, 1.0+-0.4 in Xb4b, broad-component 0.6-0.9) is HCN-rich gas or a lobe-specific blend (HDO untestable) remains undecided, so the chemistry of the outflow vs nuclei is not settled; the data cleanly establish that the outflow's dense gas is detected, subthermal (3-2/1-0 ~0.2-0.4) and not distinguishable from N/Bridge in HCN/HCO+.

(Update, p0012-r01 / p0015, supersedes the 'S cool, >=80 K excluded' reading above.) Team-b reproduced team-a's joint S fit exactly but showed that the exclusion of S Tkin>=80 K is driven by one input, the deblended S-core T43/T32 (HCN 0.268), which is not measurable at ~6" (template clip, Outer component and baseline each shift it by 0.03-0.3; p0012's own components do not reproduce the observed S aperture ratio 0.357). With matched-beam aperture or recovery-corrected ladders S allows Tkin 25-80 K (dchi2(80 K)=1.4-3.2, dchi2(100 K)=4.5-8.2). What survives is a tentative N/S T43/T32 contrast of 1.26+-0.09 (HCN, 2.9 sigma) and 1.16+-0.08 (HCO+, 2.0 sigma) in a matched 5.7x3.5" beam, with S indistinguishable from the Bridge; it cannot be separated into Tkin vs n (degenerate). Overall: N is plausibly somewhat more excited (warmer and/or denser) than S and the Bridge, n is not distinguishable, and a cool (20-30 K) S nucleus is not established; this is compatible with Pereira-Santaella+2024 (>40 K in the central 100 pc of the S outflow, a different phase) and does not conflict with the 10" result of p0011, whose circular apertures mix N and S. Tbg>5 K and IR pumping remain untested.
(Update, p0017.) Red ridge: the red-shifted dense-gas feature ~3" (~600 pc) N of S is a real, one-sided HCN/HCO+ feature (4.7/5.7 sigma over a core-matched null; the earlier 9.7/6.1 sigma are withdrawn), localized on the S axis rather than N-centred, and not a Bridge-wide strip in HCN. It is plausibly (55-65%) the receding counterpart of the S blue lobe, but its narrower profile, ~600 vs ~370 pc offset and indistinguishable r31 leave the bipolar picture unestablished; Pereira-Santaella+2024 supports bipolarity only within r<250 pc. Any dense-gas outflow budget should treat the ridge (Mdot ~3-26 Msun/yr) as conditional.

(Update, p0018.) Independent-line check of the red ridge: HCN/HCO+ 4-3 (Band 7, matched 4.5x3.0" beam, 3-2 excess as template) show only a marginal counterpart (stack 3.4 sigma, individual lines 2.3/2.9 sigma, template-dependent), with no wrong-sign signal in mirror controls; the ridge cannot be resolved from N (1.9") and S (3.3") at this beam, so Band 7 adds corroboration, not a precision measurement. The matched-beam r43/32 and HCN/HCO+ of the ridge and lobe excess are indistinguishable within 1.3 sigma, so line ratios do not separate an S counter-lobe from Bridge streaming; the ridge origin stays undecided (S counter-lobe ~55-65%). CS 7-6, SO, HC3N and H13CN limits are 4-74x above the core ratios and test nothing. The ridge mass/Mdot remain conditional on the counter-lobe hypothesis.

(Update, p0021 and replies p0007-r02, p0011-r02, p0015-r01; team-a q12c.) A second dense-gas (compact-core + envelope) component at N is neither required nor excluded. The one-zone N misfit (chi2 9.1/3, p=0.03) is acceptable (3.2/3) once beam geometry is taken from the 3-2 peak-Tb growth curve (N compact FWHM ~0.44", ~85 pc), and the Bayesian preference for two components (dlnZ +3.0 at fixed geometry) occurs in 14.5% of data-consistent one-zone simulations with wrong sizes and reverses with measured geometry. Consequently every physical scale rests on the geometry assumption: the N Tkin is unconstrained (12-96 K), team-b's Tk>~56 K (10") holds only for fixed geometry, S Tkin is ~20 K in the default deblend but deblend dependent (20-80 K), and Delta T(N-S) = +4 K [-10,+36] with P(T_N>T_S)~0.6 is unconstrained. Including the H13CN 4-3 limit as a likelihood term disfavours very thick (tau32>10), abundance-matched compact cores at N (0.03-0.11 of posterior mass) but opacity vs abundance stays open. Standing community statement: N and S differ robustly in HCN/HCO+ (0.83 vs 0.40 at 1.05"), not demonstrably in temperature or density. Conflicts resolved: where the older entries above quote N Tk >=56 K or pooled 80 K, S 'cool' or '>=80 K excluded', the q12c/p0015 values stand.

(Update, chemistry: team-b p0016 and team-a p0023, independent estimators agree.) No shock-chemistry signature is found in the nuclei at 4-6" (~0.7-1 kpc): CS 7-6/HCN 4-3 ~0.15-0.18 is uniform across N, S and Bridge, SO and other shock tracers are limits at the percent level of HCO+, and the CS/HCO+ N/S difference is an HCO+ effect (the same HCN/HCO+ contrast as above). CH3OH is the one species with a spatial signal: it is detected, cold/sub-thermal (Trot <~15-20 K, only suggestive), extended (flux plateau out to 6-9"), peaks 1-3" off both nuclei at the Bridge/W clump, and S>N only at ~3 sigma (4.6 sigma is S alone), with a S/N abundance contrast not robust to the unknown Tex/Td difference. Harada+2018's CH3OH variation is reproduced within errors when the estimator is matched (the earlier x3 tension was an artefact), so the data are consistent with, but cannot independently confirm, a shock-related CH3OH enhancement at S; our resolution (>=4.45") cannot separate N from S chemically. Harada's SiO variation cannot be tested (29SiO/30SiO limits 5-360x above Harada's SiO/CS). The N>S T43/T32 excitation contrast does not survive short-spacing correction (1.07 [0.89,1.26]), reinforcing that N-vs-S temperature/density differences are unconstrained; the robust N-vs-S difference remains HCN/HCO+ at 1".

(Update, p0024/p0006-r03.) The southern blue-lobe HCN excess is now calibrated: 4.3 sigma pointwise and ~3.2 sigma after trials correction (team-b's 6.2 sigma used a smaller noise estimate), Xb4b is consistent with it within ~1.5 sigma, and HDO as its whole origin needs HDO/HCO+~170-240 (strongly disfavoured, not excluded). The lobe is therefore a marginal, candidate HCN-rich feature of the outflow; the data do not establish an outflow-specific HCN/HCO+ enhancement (cf. Nishimura+2024) and 'dense gas, not a blend' is only medium-low confidence.

Update (p0025): the continuum-proportional spw low-edge ramp, which also sets the CH3OH blend baseline, biases HCN 4-3 integrals low by ~0-10% (central ~4%) and so HCN/HCO+ 4-3 and T43/T32 slightly low, but leaves all N/S/Bridge ladder ratios and the N-vs-S T43/T32 contrast within 1 sigma; the conclusions on HCN/HCO+ (no enhancement at S, compact N core), the unresolved N-vs-S excitation contrast and the cool off-nuclear CH3OH are unchanged. UPDATE (p0028, p0012-r02): propagating a free or bounded beam-filling factor into the 10-arcsec HCN/HCO+ ladder fits leaves the warm Tk (>~50 K, P 0.8-0.96) unchanged; filling changes opacity (tau 0.1 vs 10-100) and mass, and sub-thermal excitation versus dilution remains degenerate. A cold (20-30 K) gas filling the 10-arcsec beam is excluded, which reconciles with team-a's cool S nucleus at 1 arcsec only if that is a dilute, thick core in a warmer envelope; this reconciliation is untested. Earlier team-b tau labelled 3-2 were tau(2-1).

=== CONSOLIDATED UPDATE (synthesis 5; adds team-a p0029, p0030 and team-b p0026, p0027, p0031) ===
(A) Answer to the research question. The data separate the two nuclei (N, S), the Bridge/off-nuclear clumps and one southern blue-shifted dense-gas lobe (plus a one-sided red ridge) at 0.25-1" in Band 6, and only blended 'centre versus extended' at Band 5/7 (4-9") and for the disk. The robust, scale-independent difference is chemical/excitation in HCN relative to HCO+: HCN/HCO+ 3-2 is 0.99 at N and 0.44 at S at 50 pc (N/S 2.1+-0.2 over 50-120 pc, flat; 1.8-1.9 at 250 pc; lost at 6.5-10" by blending), with equal HCO+ T_b (2.8 K) at both nuclei, i.e. the contrast resides in HCN. The AGN-hosting S nucleus therefore has the LOWER ratio (consistent with Harada+2018: no HCN enhancement at an AGN; contrary to a naive HCN/HCO+ AGN diagnostic). No significant N-vs-S difference in density or temperature is established (T43/T32 N/S 0.97-1.24; Tk and n degenerate and prior/geometry dependent). The outflow's dense gas (S blue lobe ~370 pc S of S) is detected, subthermal, and its HCN excess is marginal (3.2-4.3 sigma); the red ridge is real in HCN (~5-6 sigma) but its origin is undecided; the N nucleus has no dense wing, as in Michiyama+2018.
(B) Cloud sizes and line widths (new). At 0.24" the nuclear dense cores are 50-100 pc across depending on the definition (Gaussian core 50-65 pc; half-max area including pedestal 80-100 pc), only marginally resolved, N elongated (~100-120 x 25 pc); HCN is as compact as or slightly more compact than HCO+ (earlier 'HCN larger' withdrawn, as is the '>=5 N sub-clumps' count); line and 1.1 mm continuum centres coincide within 0.1". Nuclear widths are sigma 50-70 km/s (intrinsic, not beam-smeared rotation), off-nuclear clumps sigma 23-28 km/s, giving M_vir ~0.3-3e8 Msun and Mdyn(<97 pc) N ~4e8, S ~1.3e8 Msun (N/S 1.4-5). Peak T_b falls 3-8x from 49 to 250 pc in every region, so the dense gas is clumpy/hierarchical, not the smooth medium Brunetti+2021 inferred from CO 2-1 (to be tested with their map). Peak T_b (2.8 K RJ, >=7 K Planck) at 50 pc and continuum T_b 0.2-0.6 K (optically thin, no absorption).
(C) Reconciling temperature statements. The 10" warm solution (Tk >~50 K, P 0.6-0.9; n < 10^5.25) describes the envelope, which holds >70-95% of the 10" 3-2 flux; the 1" S solution (17-26 K, eta_core 0.5-0.9, n~1e5, thick) describes a near space-filling 50-65 pc core that is dilute (eta~0.01) only in 1.7" apertures. These are compatible, not conflicting, but the cool S core rests on one deblend and on T_b-eta degeneracy (warm S gas with eta_core>=0.03-0.1 not excluded), and CO(2-1) T_b at S needs eta_CO>=0.5-0.9. N compact Tk is unconstrained. Where entries above give contradictory eta or N/S T43/T32 values, the p0030 aperture-referenced statement and the 1.07 [0.89,1.26] (p0022) / 0.97-1.24 (p0027) intervals stand.
(D) Still unresolved: opacity vs abundance vs excitation for the HCN deficit at S (H13CN undetected, depth insufficient); chemistry of the outflow (HDO blend untestable); origin of the red ridge; SiO and the CH3OH N/S contrast need other-band or deeper data.

Disk HCN/HCO+ update (team-a p0032, p0005-r07): the 2-1 annulus ratios (0.579/0.554/0.537/0.492 at 0-4/4-8/6-9/8-12", ~11% decline, 7-18% beam dependent) are reproduced by both teams, but the matching 3-2 8-12" ratio cannot be measured from the images (sign-changing flux, PB/zero-level dependent) and no like-for-like uv-matched test survives beyond 8". The decline is therefore not shown to be an abundance gradient; a parametric forward model needs an extra HCN 3-2 fall (eps 0.05-0.45), most plausibly excitation (low confidence). This reinforces that the disk can only be compared with the active regions at J=2-1 and at low confidence.

Disk HCN/HCO+ update (team-a p0033): independent Band 3 HCN/HCO+ 1-0 data (Michiyama, 10" beam) show an 8-12" over 4-8" decline of 6-10% (0.90-0.94 over bowl scenarios), matching the 2-1 decline of 9-11%; R21/R10 is flat within ~5% (0.95-1.01). The mild disk decline is therefore not a 2-1 imaging artifact, but both values are upper bounds (bowl at line velocities, missing short spacings), only ~2 sigma per annulus, and RADEX needs neither an abundance gradient nor an excitation change (log X +0.50 constant). The Harada 1-0 map (0.73) is not trusted at 8-12". Best reading: a weak (<=~10%) disk gradient with no demonstrated chemical or excitation origin; common-uv reimaging with short-spacing data is needed to turn the bound into a measurement. This supersedes the p0032 suggestion of a stronger 3-2 excitation fall, which stays low confidence.

J=1-0 update (team-b p0034, REVISED by p0036/p0034-r02, /snapshots/team-b-s21): adding Band 3 J=1-0 (2.2" X961 and 1.5" X145, short-spacing complete; 190-430 pc beams) and re-imaging Band 6 3-2 from visibilities (12m+7m, tapered to the same circular beams) shows that the N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast is the same at J=1-0 and 3-2: 1.47 vs 1.44 at 2.2" (D=1.00+-0.04; 1.62 vs 1.53 at 1.5"). The earlier D=1.10+-0.06 and the r31 N>S excess (HCN 1.27, HCO+ 1.13) were artefacts of 12-m flux loss in the Xb4d 3-2 image, which is larger at S (HCN +34% with the 7-m added). With uv-complete data r31 is equal at N and S (N/S 1.01 HCN, 1.03 HCO+, +-0.05) and r31(HCN)~0.26 < r31(HCO+)~0.34: no evidence for an excitation difference between the nuclei, while the lower HCN/HCO+ at the AGN-hosting S nucleus is present at both J. RADEX Bayes factors weakly favour abundance-only over excitation-only (ln BF +1.0 vs +0.2; difference <1, not decisive). The S blue-lobe HCN/HCO+ 3-2 excess (1.2-1.4) is not reproduced in 1-0 (0.59+-0.11; 2.6-3.3 sigma statistical, S-wing leakage possible), so a lobe-specific HCN excess is unsupported at this resolution (tempering the p0024 lobe-excess result). H13CO+/HCO+ 0.023 gives HCO+ 1-0 tau ~1-2 (12C/13C 40-100 assumed) and, with LVG, tilts moderately (ln BF 2.3-3.9, prior dependent) towards common excitation with ~2x higher HCN/HCO+ column ratio at N than S (2-2.5 sigma). SiO/HCO+ is 1.6x higher at S (marginal N detection) and HC3N/HCN slightly higher at S: 1-2 sigma-class. The earlier 1.0" X94a S>N r31 reversal and an N tau=9-15 fit are retracted (recovery artefact / fit artefact); X94a (12m only) loses 30-50% flux and is used for ratios only.

Continuum dependence and excitation vs abundance (team-a p0035, /snapshots/team-a-s16; confirmed by p0034-r01): the inward rise of HCN/HCO+ 3-2 in N (0.30 at 2-3" to ~1 at the core, 0.30" beam; 0.40 to 0.81 at 1.05") is a property of the N nucleus, not a function of continuum surface brightness: S stays flat at ~0.4 although its core 258 GHz continuum is stronger (1.6 vs 0.6 mJy/beam), and at equal HCO+ brightness N and S differ (R 0.63 vs 0.43). Pooled pixel regression with a nucleus indicator finds no significant dependence on continuum (std. coeff +0.05 vs null 0.00+-0.05); within N alone there is a ~2 sigma, radius-degenerate rise. Velocity-resolved R is flat (no opacity/self-absorption signature), HCN v2=1f is <3% of v=0 (no IR pumping signature), and RADEX shows R~1 is the thick/thermalised ceiling; at fixed ladders only a x3-4 higher HCN/HCO+ abundance ratio (or HCO+ deficit) reproduces N, so abundance rather than excitation is favoured, consistent with the equal N/S contrast at 1-0 and 3-2 (uv-matched) and the H13CO+ tilt. The lower R at the AGN-hosting S nucleus argues against an X-ray/AGN-driven HCN enhancement there, in line with Harada+2018 (no HCN/HCO+ enhancement at the AGN). H40a (Band 3) is consistent with predominantly free-free (f_ff 0.6-0.7 at 98 GHz, S 2.4-3.3 sigma, N 1.5 sigma; low confidence, Michiyama+2020 deeper detection consistent); the 98-258 GHz decomposition makes N ~70-80% dust at 1.1 mm and the S core only 35-45% dust (low confidence). Whether N is HCN-rich or HCO+-poor remains open (team-b p0038 Q35, team-a p0007-r04 agree): the N/S HCN/HCO+ ratio is 1.5-1.9 at 1-0, 3-2 and 4-3 and ~2 in the H13CN/H13CO+ thin limit (weak), but the N nucleus is more excited in CS (5-4/2-1 N/S 1.57) and C18O (2-1/1-0 1.48) than in HCN or HCO+ (r31 N/S 1.16/0.90), so normalising by a J-mismatched reference flips the sign. With excitation-corrected CS columns N is HCO+-poor (HCO+/CS N/S 0.63 [0.47,0.84]; HCN/CS 1.04); with CS 2-1 or C18O 1-0 it is HCN-rich (1.5-1.6, HCO+ flat); the HCO+/continuum deficit is 2.8 sigma (MC) and 0.52-0.64 after free-free correction, not the earlier 4 sigma, and a single gas fits the CS ladder poorly at N (chi2 10, ~0 dof), so no reference is trusted; the starburst-chemistry, cosmic-ray and HCO+ destruction options are not discriminated.
caveats: CH3OH Q-branch blend integral at Xb55: with the spw22 edge ramp modelled (p0020) the baseline systematic is +-14-37% (N 1.13, S 1.61, Bridge 1.69, W 0.72 Jy/b km/s), down from a factor 2-4; the ramp shape under the line (ch 120-190) is extrapolated and is now the dominant systematic (ramp vs quadratic baselines differ up to 2x at N); the ramp mechanism is inferred (no uv data) and rests on two spws at one edge. Any line near a low spw edge in Xb55 spw18/22, Xb4f spw18 or Xb47 spw16 near bright continuum needs the same treatment.
Soutflow and disk are candidates; HOC+, SO/CH3OH A-cluster tentative; 176.011 and 341.928 GHz unassigned.

Systemic velocity 2780 km/s is a single adopted value; nuclear peak velocities differ by ~100 km/s at 0.25" (N 2811-2817, S 2710), so +-350 km/s windows are not centred on each nucleus; the HCN/HCO+ integrals use the same fixed window for both lines.

Line identifications rest on Splatalogue CDMS/JPL rest frequencies at v=2780 km/s; HOC+, SO 4_5-3_4 and both unidentified features need independent confirmation (e.g. matching J transitions at matched beam).
The Band-5 cubes do not separate N, S, Bridge (13% leakage at the nuclear separation, single HCO+ 2-1 peak pixel).
Empirical noise comes from emission-free pixels at 6-11" (primary-beam-corrected noise there is 1.2-1.6x the central value), which makes limits conservative by up to ~1.5x.
Xb4b nuclear emission is clumpy: peak-pixel values depend on the exact pixel chosen (search radius 1"); spectra are non-Gaussian (double-horned), Gaussian FWHM are indicative only.
No source of data for line-free-channel continuum from cubes exists (cubes are continuum-subtracted); the contamination check relies on mfs vs cont images, which have 1-2 sigma noise.
The 'aperture' (1.5" radius) rows of the line table use statistical noise only (no empirical null).
The conversion to K km/s uses the Rayleigh-Jeans formula with the beam of each cube; distance 40 Mpc is only used for pc sizes.

CH3OH LTE/RADEX fits have chi2/dof ~9-11: the numbers Trot=9 K and n>=1e7 are formal; the robust statement is 'Q-branch J>=4 absent: low excitation'. Baseline ripple of ~0.2 K km/s is visible in Band 5 (J=5 at -4 sigma).
Local-velocity matching (not 2780 km/s) is essential for identifications at S (2710-2740 km/s): at vsys the 251.66 feature would favour NS; at local velocity it clearly favours CH3OH.

The zero level of Xb4f/Xb55 moment-0 maps at r>8" is biased by about -0.5 / -1.3 Jy/b km/s (negative bowl, missing short spacings); disk fluxes are zero-level-corrected with the r=14-22" ring and carry >=0.3 Jy/b km/s systematic.

Soutflow position error is dominated by the assumed 10% beam pointing floor (0.10"), not by the fit (0.01-0.02"); wing definition relative to v_S=2722; comparison with the CO outflow geometry (Sakamoto+2014, Michiyama+2018) has not been made quantitatively.
H13CN limit conditional on the CO-wing family; log-quadratic/cubic wings can absorb a genuine H13CN signal.
Literature cross-check is from abstracts/summaries (Harada+2018, Sato+2022), not their tables.
Team conflict resolved: single systemic velocity 2780 km/s (team-a) replaced by per-region velocities (team-b); N-S offset +71+-28 km/s.

Blue-wing fluxes are lower limits because the pipeline clean mask misses high-velocity channels (0.4-0.65% of pixels); the HCN wing flux differs between teams (0.33 vs 0.15) owing to window/aperture choices.

CH3OH: ID of 254 GHz rests on one transition plus velocity (10 km/s systematic floor); the J=1-3 blend amplitude has a +-14-37% ramp-baseline systematic (p0020; team-a's 2.0-2.2 is above the range); the Q-branch excess is single-team; Xb4d/Xb4f flux recovery is not controlled with HCO+; a Band-7 second transition does not exist in the data.
HOC+, SO 4_5-3_4 (Band 5), HC3N, HC15N, H41beta and CH3CN are marginal or single-frequency identifications; SO 6_5-5_4 is not in the data; unassigned lines at 176.011 and 341.928 GHz (team-a) remain.
Distance (40 Mpc) and literature statements are taken from abstracts only and are assumptions of results involving physical sizes and comparison with Michiyama, Harada, Brunetti, Nishimura.

Flux-recovery fractions are relative to Xb4f only; no total-power data, so true missing flux is unknown (lower limits). Beam-area rescaling assumes smooth emission; negative bowls make Xb4b r>=12" sums unphysical; pb correction at r=8-12" not in the error budget.
Native-beam peak-pixel intensities in the inventory are not beam matched across OUS; use the matched-beam ratio results for any comparison.
Disk: one 2-1 tracer; zero-level correction changes the 3-2 ratio by ~4; uv coverage (B_min 8.7 m) inferred from beam sizes only; missing flux vs low excitation degenerate.
Soutflow wing HCN/HCO+ depends on window and estimator (1.2-1.8); comparison with the CO outflow geometry and quantitative matching to Michiyama+2018 not yet made.
Still untested: Soutflow vs CO outflow geometry, matched-beam ladders with a second independent team, cloud sizes/linewidths.

p0005 (team-b): the 8-12" disk ratio carries a zero-level systematic up to +-0.1 because the far-field bowl is not flat (17-24" ring negative); the 12% decline is therefore ~1-2 sigma if the full systematic is used.

Sblue wing ratio is window-dependent (-350..-100 km/s gives 1.02+-0.18 as core HCO+ leaks in); Xb4b HCN wing flux is only 53% of Xb4d (partly resolved out), so the blue-wing R relies on one array for R>1.
Team-b injection tests show deblended S/N ratios carry 15-25% template bias (S coefficient biased high); 2-1 N/S contrast remains unconstrained.

Outflow dense-gas ratio: the Soutflow blue-lobe HCN/HCO+ depends on aperture, window centre and array (Xb4d 1.24 vs Xb4b-smoothed 1.00; peak-selected 1.7 biased); Xb4b resolves out extended flux (ratios 15-25% lower); HDO blend untestable; Michiyama+2018 1-0 fluxes and Sakamoto+2014 CO masses are literature assumptions; CO-kinematics comparison and a tilted-ring/tidal alternative remain untested.

H13CN injection-recovery noise has no CO-wing structure; wing-family degeneracy (alpha shifts ~0.05) is not fully captured, and the tau/core bounds depend on the assumed 12C/13C (30-100) and a 15% Band 6 vs 7 flux scale.
Settling opacity vs abundance at the N core needs H13CN or H13CO+ 3-2/4-3 at <0.5" or HNC; none are covered by 2017.1.00379.S products.

p0008: absolute flux loss of each array cannot be measured from image products (no visibilities or total power); recovery numbers are relative to Xb4f and depend on assumed uv coverage and MRS ratio. The sign of R55/R4f and R47/R4f is prior-dominated. E2 and HCN clump recoveries are unconstrained; Gaussian-clump assumption; Xb47 field ends before its bowl closes.

p0010: wing ratios beyond ~150 km/s are noise-limited in one line (limits only); residual 0.02-0.03 per 100 km/s slope unexplained (finer gradient or HCN-wing blends, CH3NH2 on red HCN unquantified); 6.5" N/S ladder model chi2/dof 6-16; RADEX single-zone, unreliable above tau~1e3.

RADEX (p0011, p0009): single-zone, beam-averaged, LVG, equal-filling unless stated; Tk upper end and n lower end are prior-set; flat n priors above 1e7 are dominated by a cold dense thin branch excluded only on physical arguments (Tdust, CO Tb); the compact 1.7" and 10" ladders cannot share one zone at N (chi2 9.2+14.0); team-a fits use a physT30 prior (Tkin>=30 K) and a different beam, so Tk values are not directly comparable.

J=1-0 inputs are literature values at 1.7" (Harada+2018 Table 13 parsed from arXiv HTML, Michiyama+2018) with different uv coverage and flux scale; our and Harada 3-2 integrals differ by 4-23% per line; missing extended 1-0 flux would bias R10 and the 60%/40% split.
E1 vs centre contrast rests on shared calibration, the E1 HCN 4-3 primary-beam/A-B systematic (17-34%) and ACA recovery; E2 and W are unconstrained; no total-power data exist.
Resolving opacity vs abundance needs H13CN/H13CO+ at <0.5" (alpha<~0.03), HNC, or J=1-0 cubes; N vs S excitation needs matched ~2-6" ladders with deblending or sub-arcsec higher-J data.

Q2 (p0012): one-zone RADEX, equal-weight pooling of classes A/B/F2 is a choice; N is fitted poorly (HCN 3-2/2-1 0.35 is 2.8 sigma below every class); S result conditional on Tbg<=5 K; grid has a 10 K edge and 0.25 dex steps; Tbg modelled as blackbody and an unresolved hot dust core is not excluded; no IR-pumping model; hyperfine structure not modelled.

Q2 N-vs-S temperature contrast is suggestive only; Bridge, disk, wing and outflow temperatures are unconstrained (2 data vs 3 parameters). Harada+2018 1-0 inputs are literature values at 1.7" (assumption).

Soutflow (p0013): excess is uncleaned residual flux present in Xb4d (clean mask empty at -405..-205 km/s), only 1.0 sigma in Xb4b; Xb4b/Xb4d difference 2.0 sigma; wing-ratio values depend on the velocity frame (1.04-1.68) and a-posteriori aperture; HDO blend cannot be tested with in-band lines; N wing limits at 350-750 km/s are baseline-limited.

S-lobe mass and Mdot rest on a single-zone RADEX fit that fails the HCN 3-2/1-0 ratio (2.6 sigma), an assumed X(HCO+) (1e-9 to 1e-8) and an assumed inclination; they are order-of-magnitude (1.5 dex). Lobe wing fluxes are uncleaned residual-dominated and differ between Xb4d and Xb4b for HCN by a factor ~2. Deeper Band 3/7 cleaned imaging or an HDO line outside these spws would decide blend vs HCN-rich gas.

Revision caveat (p0012-r01): all S-nucleus Tkin statements rest on the S-core ladder, which is deblend-dependent; team-a had not answered the team-b reproduction at the time of this synthesis, so the revision adopts team-b's matched-aperture values because they are measured directly in a defined beam, whereas the deblended core values could not be reproduced. Confirming a real N/S excitation difference needs the J=4 and J=3 data at a common beam with higher S/N or J=1-0 at matched resolution.

Red ridge origin (S counter-lobe vs Bridge streaming) is undecided: no line-independent test (H13CN, CS 7-6, SO at the ridge), only 3-6 brightness-matched null controls, no CO/JWST velocity-sign map beyond 250 pc; r31 limited by the Michiyama+2018 flux scale.

p0018: the 4-3 ridge detection is ~3 sigma and depends on the 3-2 template and taper; Band 7 beam (4.1x2.7") blends N, S and ridge; H13CN 4-3 sits on the CO 3-2 tail (negative formal excess); weak-line limits are too shallow (would need >10x lower noise). Resolving the origin needs a velocity-sign map of CO/JWST beyond 250 pc or deeper data.
CH3OH off-nuclear enhancement rests on one transition (254 GHz) at 3-4 sigma; no second low-Eu transition exists at <=4" resolution, so the N/S contrast is data-limited.

q12c (p0021): the 1-0 point is a literature value at 1.7" (Harada+2018) and N and S blend there; the 2-1/4-3 compact sizes are unmeasurable (Band 5/7 beams 4.5-9") and the relative size scatter (0.15, 0.30) is assumed; models are one- and two-zone LVG spheres with shared Tbg 2.73 K (5 K as test); Tbg>5 K, IR pumping and the range of S P(T>=80 K) over deblend variants were not tested.

Chemistry: SiO (and HC3N 10-9) need ~10-20x deeper or other-band data; a short-spacing-complete CH3OH map at <=2" and an independent Tex(N) vs Tex(S) (e.g. CH3OH 241.79 GHz) are needed to decide whether the CH3OH abundance contrast between S and N is real.

The T43/T32 recovery correction rests on a prior-dependent Xb47/Xb4f short-spacing loss (Bmin); array types are inferred from beams, not visibilities. CH3OH S>N (~3 sigma) and the Harada comparison (~30% errors) are marginal.

HCN 4-3 (Xb47) and HCN 3-2 (Xb4f) quoted integrals and 4-3-based ratios are raw values; add ~+4+-4% (N), +6+-5% (S), +6+-4% (Bridge) for HCN 4-3 per p0025. The ramp extent under the red wing cannot be measured without visibilities and also affects the red-ridge channels (+250..+350 km/s).

Team-b's earlier 'tau(HCN 3-2)' values (s62/s64/s66/s104) were tau(2-1) (corrected in s108); use tau(3-2)=5.9 [0.2,57] and tau(4-3)=1.0 for the flat-eta N fit. The 10" cold-gas exclusion and the 1" cool-S result use overlapping apertures/deblends and are not independent; confirmation needs a two-component model or J=1-0 / H13CN at matched resolution.

Core sizes are definition dependent (Gaussian core 50-65 pc vs half-max 80-100 pc) and the cores are only 0.2-0.4 beam resolved; anything below ~0.1" is an upper limit. The Brunetti+2021 CO(2-1) T_b/smoothness comparison uses abstract/Table 2 values (arXiv HTML), not their cube.

The cool S core (17-26 K, eta 0.5-0.9) is a conditional, tentative result: it depends on the 1.7" 4-3/3-2 deblend, an assumed core size and X(HCN)>~1e-8; the 10" warm envelope result is calibration/Tbg dependent (P(T>50 K)=0.6-0.9).

Red-ridge HCN significance depends on the red-side baseline (+-0.05 on 0.126 Jy/beam km/s, because all line-free channels of the Xb4d HCN cube lie blue of the line); HCO+ is only 2-4 sigma and the 4-3 counterpart is unconstrained.
Disk HCN/HCO+ (p0032): 8-12" 3-2 ratio unmeasurable from image products; only re-imaging the raw data with a common uv range (7-m only) plus total power would remove the recovery degeneracy.

J=1-0 comparison (p0034/p0036) is at 1.5-2.2" (190-430 pc) vs 0.95" native for the 3-2 cubes, so the 50-120 pc N/S 3-2 contrast (2.0-2.1) has no 1-0 counterpart; the Band 6 re-imaging used only 1 of 2 12-m and 3 of 14 7-m EBs, and Band 3 visibilities could not be restored (X961/X145 no manifest; X94a 57.7 GB), so the 1-0 side is matched in beam and short-spacing completeness only, not in identical uv range. Independent 12C/13C and deeper lobe weak-line data are still needed; the S-lobe 1-0 vs 3-2 comparison was not redone with uv-complete 3-2; HCN hyperfines unmodelled and RADEX is one-zone. Earlier 3-2 Xb4d-only ratios/r31 at >=1.5" apertures carry a 12-m flux-loss bias.

p0035 continuum-dependence test: the N-nucleus partial continuum dependence is degenerate with radius; 1.05" null uses only 3 shifts; H40a is only 1.5-3.3 sigma (4-8x shallower than Michiyama+2020) with Te/LTE assumed; outer-S continuum decomposition rejects 5-73% of draws; common-uv spectral index cannot be built from image products; HCN-rich vs HCO+-poor N is unresolved (HCN profile steepness vs CS/HCN vs CS/HCO+). Beam-matched J=1-0 and 3-2 analysis remains the cleanest way to test abundance vs excitation.

Q35 (team-b p0038, team-a p0007-r04): the Harada 1.7" and Xb47 4.3" sets are not on one beam (Harada cubes unavailable); CS is not a faithful abundance reference at N (one-gas CS ladder fit fails, chi2 10 for ~0 dof); free-free (5-20% of 346 GHz continuum) and N-vs-S dust temperature/opacity are unconstrained; 12C/13C is assumed for H13CN/H13CO+ columns. A J-independent thin column tracer at the same J or a resolved H13CN/H13CO+ 3-2 or 4-3 would decide it.
